transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-03 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood); Ravi, Aisha, Dana, Tom (Casbah)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Intro discovery: Casbah wants to move from research sandbox to a production-safe deployment path; evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Main concerns: latency SLOs for clinical assistant, PHI handling, SOC2 + KMS, timeline to first real request.
- Agreed next steps: sandbox access + credits, baseline perf runs, security deep dive.

Topics detected: deployment fit, time-to-first-token, pilot scope, security/compliance, cost-latency trade-offs.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, our AE, and this is Liam, our solutions engineer. how are you all?
[00:05] Ravi: good, thanks. ran out of coffee but, um, excited to dig in.
[00:08] Aisha: morning all — Aisha here. we tried a couple of open models in-house, but want to understand the path to production without, like, rebuilding serving.
[00:16] Maya: perfect — that's exactly what we help with. quick agenda: understand your current stack, constraints, success metrics; show how Hosted/Dedicated/Private map to those; next steps for a sandbox and pilot. sound good?
[00:25] Tom: yes, brief from my side — product wants a clinical triage assistant, low-latency conversational flow, sometimes needs to load EHR context 1-2k tokens. primary metric is p95 under 600ms for short responses, but for longer context, acceptable up to 1.2s.
[00:40] Dana: and security is non-negotiable — PHI flows, keys must be customer-managed, audit logs, SSO/SAML, and we need SOC2 evidence.
[00:48] Liam: okay noted. quick clarifying q — is the EHR context going to be sent as embeddings + retrieval or raw context on every request?
[00:54] Aisha: plan is retrieval: we store vectorized notes and fetch top-k; then we send ~1-2 chunks so typical request lengths vary 200–1,200 tokens. sometimes we do multi-round chat with KV cache.
[01:06] Liam: great, that lines up with what Redwood Optimize and the runtime can do — prefix caching and KV cache reduce repeated cost for multi-turn.
[01:12] Maya: for the deployment modes — Hosted is quickest: API keys, free credits to evaluate, self-serve. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation. Private is VPC/on-prem for full control and customer-managed KMS.
[01:24] Ravi: timeline? we want a pilot in ~4 weeks to validate latency and safety checks. can hosted hit our p95 numbers or do we need dedicated?
[01:34] Liam: depends on model and sequence distribution. for chat with 512 tokens average, our benchmark on a single A100-ish dedicated pool hits p95 ~420ms with optimized kernels and batching disabled for low-latency. Hosted can match that on equivalent capacity but bursts are subject to multi-tenant throttles unless you pick a higher tier.
[01:50] Tom: we can't have unpredictable throttles — clinical assistant needs consistent experience.
[01:54] Maya: understood. a common pattern: start with Hosted sandbox for time-to-first-token and functional evals (fast), then move to Dedicated pilot (reserved pool) for guaranteed SLOs. Private is typical for later-stage deployments with strict KMS/residency.
[02:06] Dana: what about data retention on Hosted? PHI on the request payload — we need logs off by default and customer-managed encryption.
[02:13] Maya: Hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit; for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private. Hosted can be configured with no-persist mode and ephemeral logs for the sandbox — we'll put that in the quickstart.
[02:23] Aisha: can you walk through the sandbox flow for an engineer: how long to first token? I've seen numbers like 10–30 minutes in other vendors.
[02:31] Liam: typical flow: sign up, we provision org + API key, import a sample prompts repo, run a sample chat. with our free credits and starter templates, devs get a first response in under 10 minutes if they follow the quickstart. for integrated EHR retrieval tests you're looking at a day or two to wire up vector DB stubs.
[02:49] Ravi: that speed is good. what about costs — cost per 1k tokens in Hosted vs Dedicated?
[02:55] Maya: Hosted is usage-based; costs vary by model tier. Dedicated is lower unit cost at scale because you commit capacity — typically 20–40% cheaper at predictable volumes. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batch profiles to reduce tokens per dollar.
[03:09] Tom: question on model updates: we need canary rollouts and immediate rollback if hallucination rate spikes.
[03:16] Liam: rollouts are supported — console supports per-route model pinning, canary percentages, and automatic fallback to a safer variant. we also do quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and can alert on regressions.
[03:26] Dana: auditability — can we get per-token tracing and who-called-what?
[03:30] Liam: yes, Redwood Console has traces and per-token cost breakdowns. for Private we can stream audit logs to your SIEM.
[03:36] [00:03:45] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[03:40] Aisha: for the pilot, we want to run a baseline test — 1k requests/min, chiefly 512 tokens, and measure p50/p95/p99, plus cost projections. can Redwood provide a template?
[03:50] Maya: yes — Liam will share a benchmark template with run scripts. we can also run a Redwood-hosted baseline run if you provide a representative prompt set and sample DB.
[03:59] Liam: note — quantization affects latency but also quality; for clinical content we usually recommend FP16 or 8-bit with evals. we'll include quantization tradeoff notes.
[04:10] Ravi: about KMS — hosted MDK isn't acceptable, we need customer-managed KMS for keys used to encrypt data at rest. is that supported?
[04:18] Maya: Dedicated and Private support customer KMS. Hosted can support bring-your-own-key for certain enterprise tiers; we'll include exact options in the security packet.
[04:27] Dana: SOC2 — do you maintain reports we can share with auditors?
[04:31] Maya: yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II; we can share the attestation and control mappings. for Private/on-prem we help with artifact collection.
[04:39] Tom: any hidden dependencies for Private deployment? like specific networking or hardware procurement timelines?
[04:44] Liam: Private typically needs a few things: network peering config (VPCs), minimum GPU profile (we have supported footprints), and an on-prem install window. timeline often 6–10 weeks depending on procurement.
[04:55] Aisha: that rules out Private for our 4-week pilot — so we'll focus Hosted->Dedicated path.
[04:59] Maya: that makes sense. we often do Hosted sandbox for functional checks and then spin up a small Dedicated pool for the pilot (1–2 GPUs) to validate SLOs.
[05:07] Ravi: okay. security walkthrough — will Dana need to see network diagrams and KMS integration docs?
[05:13] Maya: yes — we'll send a security pack: SOC2, network diagrams, KMS patterns, audit log examples, and a checklist for pre-onboarding.
[05:20] Dana: also we need RBAC and SSO: SAML/SCIM for provisioning.
[05:24] Liam: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC is configurable. we'll include sample policies.
[05:29] Tom: one last product q: how do you handle model fallbacks during outages?
[05:33] Liam: smart routing — fallback to a cheaper or small model variant in the same compatibility group, or route to a different region. can configure percent-based fallback.
[05:39] Aisha: do you have rate limiting and quotas per API key?
[05:42] Maya: yes, per-key quotas and rate limits; on Dedicated we can set token ceilings at pool-level.
[05:47] Ravi: what's the onboarding for ML engineers — is there an SE-led workshop?
[05:50] Maya: yeah we do a 90-120 minute technical kickoff with your engineers to run the quickstart, run a sample perf test, and go through telemetry. we'll include that as an option.
[06:00] Tom: cost control — can we retroactively see token breakdown per route so product can optimize prompts?
[06:05] Liam: yes, Console includes per-route token-level cost breakdown and a token heatmap for prompts.
[06:09] [00:06:12] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[06:12] Aisha: safety controls for hallucinations: do you have a builtin reranker or verification plug-in?
[06:17] Liam: we provide reranking and re-check steps, and you can integrate programmatic checks. Redwood Optimize can recommend a rerank+verify step for high-risk outputs.
[06:25] Dana: good — we'll want to see how the reranker affects latency.
[06:29] Maya: we'll include an expected latency delta table in the benchmark template.
[06:33] Ravi: ok recap — we want: sandbox access + free credits, quickstart repo, benchmark template, security pack, and a short SE workshop.
[06:41] Maya: yep. and we'll propose pilot scope: 4 weeks, dedicated pool, target p95 <=600ms for 512-token chat, run accuracy/regression evals on your prompt set.
[06:52] Tom: agreed. I'll confirm product stakeholders and timeline by Friday.
[06:56] Aisha: I'll send a sanitized prompt set and sample retrieval traces.
[07:00] Dana: I'll assemble SOC2 checklist and KMS requirements, send over next week.
[07:04] Maya: perfect. Liam and I will follow up with links and scheduling.
[07:08] [00:07:10] Speaker 1: thanks all, bye.

End of call.
